name: Chime Financial, Inc.
moat_justification: Primary-account direct-deposit base of 10.4M active members and an owned processing stack (ChimeCore) behind an 88-89% gross margin, but core interchange economics rent the Durbin small-issuer exemption through partner banks, consumer switching costs are low, and there is no through-cycle ROIC record (roic_proxy distorted by negative pre-IPO equity and the FY2025 IPO SBC catch-up).
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 93.4%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
THIN_HISTORY: only 3 fiscal years of data

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low

IRR_AT_FLOOR: implied IRR sits within 0.5pp of terminal growth 2.5% (super_bear) — a perpetuity growing at g has an IRR above g at any price, so the model cannot express a return below ~2.5%; this price is beyond the model's range and the expected return is 'at most ~3.0%', not the recorded figure
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 0.3% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile
one_liner: Fast-growing neobank with an 89% gross margin but almost no owner's earnings after real SBC — moat 4/10, weighted IRR 3.3%, IV@15% $1.55 vs $29.67; does not clear 15% until ~$1.55.
moat_for: 10.4M active members with primary-account direct-deposit relationships — the paycheck anchor in mass-market consumer finance
Highest engagement in the category; ChimeCore owned processing stack with company-estimated ~60% lower transaction processing cost
Gross margin 82.8% → 87.6% → 88.0% → 88.7% TTM — high and rising
Brand leadership in the underbanked segment
moat_against: About two-thirds of revenue is interchange priced off the Durbin small-bank exemption — a regulatory loophole, not an owned asset
No bank charter of its own in the filing period; deposits and issuance sit with Stride / Bancorp partner banks
Low consumer switching costs vs Cash App, SoFi, Dave, Current and incumbent banks
Member base is the most employment- and spend-cyclical segment; new lending (MyPay, Instant Loans) imports untested credit risk
No clean year of ROIC above the cost of capital on the filed record
